Title: kiro chats on the page and on the screen
Approach: kiro-cli 2.27.1's `--v3` sessions are files, not rows in `data.sqlite3` (which holds auth and history only): the binary names `KIRO_HOME/.kiro/sessions/<workspace bucket>/sess_<uuid>/` with `session.json` and `messages.jsonl`. chat.py reads a kiro conversation from that `messages.jsonl` as a `READERS` entry (found by session id under `$KIRO_HOME/.kiro/sessions`, not by `dfs_context.transcript_path`, which returns a chain's run log for kiro). run.sh `--chat-turn` under kiro runs `kiro-cli chat --v3 --output-format stream-json --no-interactive [--resume-id <sid>] <prompt>`, stderr included, and chat.py `--kiro-result` reads the stream into the one JSON line a turn is read from (`sessionId` from the ACP events, the answer from `runFinished.finalText` or the `agent_message_chunk`s). The screen's `c` opens a new kiro chat as codex's does (opening turn headless, id recorded, then `kiro-cli chat --v3 --resume-id <sid>`). Tests with a kiro stub in test_chat.py.
Hypothesis: A kiro session's `messages.jsonl` holds one message a line with a user or assistant role and its text, under `$KIRO_HOME/.kiro/sessions/<bucket>/<session id>/`, and a turn's stream ends in `runFinished.finalText`. Wrong if a real kiro-cli session keeps its messages elsewhere or in a shape the reader finds no user and assistant text in, so the page shows no kiro messages though the turns ran.
Evidence:
for: the kiro-cli-chat binary (2.27.1) names `KIRO_HOME/.kiro/sessions`, `sess_<uuid>` ids, `session.json` (schemaVersion 1.0.0), `messages.jsonl`, and message payload kinds assistant, tool_call, tool_result and steer; `data.sqlite3` here has only migrations, history, state and auth_kv tables.

Determination: A kiro chat works on the page and on the screen against a stand-in kiro: the conversation is read from `messages.jsonl`, the turn runs `kiro-cli chat --v3 --output-format stream-json --no-interactive [--resume-id <sid>] -- <prompt>` read by `chat.py --kiro-result`, and the screen's opening turn runs headless then resumes; test_chat (45), test_web, test_ptyrelay, test_webscreen, test_walker, test_chain, test_kiro and test_opencode pass, but no real kiro session was read, since no login exists here.

text:
Title: Fix: landing a merged pull request commits on local main, so the next landing cannot fast-forward
Approach: `github.land` fast-forwards the default branch to `<remote>/<default>` and then commits the task's log there (`_commit_task_files(task, work_root, "the pull request is merged")`), never pushing it, so after every landing local main is one commit ahead of the remote (test_chain's end-to-end test shows `git log hub/master..master` = "W1: the pull request is merged"). The next pull request merged on GitHub that does not carry that commit (one opened before the landing, or any squash/rebase merge) cannot be fast-forwarded: `land` raises asking the author to run `git pull --ff-only <remote> <default>`, which fails too ("Diverging branches can't be fast-forwarded"), and the task stays unlanded with its worktree. Reproduced by committing a local-only `.dfs/items/W0.md` on main before `merge_on_github` + `watch`: the raise is logged and the advised pull exits 128. Choose how the landing log reaches the remote or is reconciled (push it, rebase local-only roadmap commits onto the fetched default branch, or keep the log off main until the author pushes) so that two pull requests landed in a row both land, and add a test_chain test that lands two merged pull requests in turn, one squash-merged.
Determination: When the default branch cannot be fast-forwarded to the merged pull request because commits only here sit in the way (an earlier landing's log, the author's unpushed work), `github.land` replays them on the remote's default branch (`git rebase --rebase-merges`, with `-X ours` when only `.dfs` files clash), pushes nothing, and raises with `git pull --rebase` only when something else clashes; a new `test_chain` test lands two pull requests in turn, the second squash-merged, over an unpushed author commit, and `test_chain`, `test_github`, `test_tree`, `test_walker` and `test_walk` pass.

Approach: W74.4 made the drag timer in `scripts/web/index.html` (the `pointerdown` handler) scroll up while the pointer is above `room = Math.max(90, walkbox bottom + 30)`. Title: Fix: concurrent moves may reach the server out of send order, and a late reply can overwrite the chats view's state
Approach: In `moveTask` (scripts/web/index.html) send each `/api/order` request only after the previous one has been answered (a promise chain `SENDING`), so the server (which applies a move under `LOCK` in arrival order) sees moves in send order and the reply to the last one sent is the list after all of them; the earlier assumption that replies arrive in send order becomes true by construction. Determination: Confirmed: moves are now written one request at a time so the server applies them in send order, and a late reply no longer overwrites the state of a view that has left the task list; reorder, reorderpending and reorderbreak pass, and the ui suite shows only the five failures the base commit has.
